title: Segment-based canaries with drift-aware rollback and latency budget gates for pinned revisions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We need a predictable, safe way to promote pinned model revisions to production while catching subtle distributional shifts and preserving latency SLOs. Proposal: implement a segment-based canary orchestration that directs small, orthogonal traffic cohorts (by region, vertical, client-tier, or deterministic hash of user id) to a new pinned revision. Combine this with drift-aware checks that compare embedding distributions and top-token divergence, and latency budget gates that abort or throttle rollout when tail latency exceeds configured budgets. The system should publish a per-revision performance profile (latency P50/P95/P99, token throughput, cost/token) and enforce KPI contracts (error rate, hallucination proxy, helpfulness score) before increasing traffic. Rollback and fallback policies must be automated and integrate with pin-aware routing so that a pinned customer sees either the previous revision or a staged fallback variant.

acceptance_criteria: Can configure cohort selectors (region, customer_tier, client_id hash) and initial weights per pinned revision
Performance profile published automatically for each pinned revision (P50/P95/P99 latency, tokens/sec, cost/token)
Drift detection metrics (embedding KL divergence, top-5 token distribution shift) computed and surfaced for canary cohorts
Automatic gates: block traffic ramp if latency P95 exceeds budget OR drift exceeds threshold OR KPI-contracts are violated
Rollout console page shows cohort weights, live KPI trends, and one-click rollback to previous revision
Integration tests exercising rollback triggers and fallback routing for pinned customers
Runbook and playbook published with automated alert thresholds and on-call steps
